clue.text: A long way from America: they fly back

indicators.note: back says the letters of the air force are read in reverse order

parts.note: the RAF, Britain's Royal Air Force, are the ones who fly

explanation.surface: Something far from America, perhaps migrating birds heading home.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at a great distance is said to be far off, so this adverb is a synonym for being a long way.

clue.text: Test alcohol-free beer at the end (European one)

parts.note: a dry event or place serves no alcohol

indicators.note: at the end picks only the final letter of the word beer

parts.note: un is French for one, a European language's word

explanation.surface: A trial of non-alcoholic beer, with a European brew brought in at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal or trial run before the real thing is a common idiom for a test.

clue.text: Orders sidecar after pub shuts

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: orders as a verb means puts into a new arrangement, so the letters of sidecar are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A customer orders a Sidecar cocktail just after the pub closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orders' rearranges SIDECAR into RICADES, placed after BAR. 'shuts' looks like a pub closing, but it is the verb defined.
explanation.definitionFit: To block an entrance with obstacles is to close it off, so the verb works as a synonym for shuts.

clue.text: French number went down, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: a ship that went down sank

explanation.surface: A French figure dropped, according to report.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for five, a number in that language, is pronounced much like the English sank.

clue.text: Like some crisps? Nuts? Deal with change

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A bar snack question: crisps or nuts? Sort it out with your change.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain crisps come without added salt, so the adjective describes a variety of crisp.

clue.text: Wine cocktails shaken the wrong way?

indicators.note: cocktails are shaken, and here the letters of the two words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Were the wine cocktails shaken in the wrong direction?
explanation.definitionFit: Turning opposite to the hands of a clock is the wrong way round for a clock, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Lines blocked with empty Eurostar coaches

indicators.note: blocked with says the outer word is filled with the other letters

parts.note: trains can mean lines or series, as in a train of thought

indicators.note: empty removes the inside of Eurostar, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Rail lines obstructed by empty Eurostar carriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaches' suggests railway carriages, matching Eurostar, but it means sports coaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports instructors who train athletes are coaches, so the plural noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Bases recipe off Black Russians once

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: off means the letter for recipe is removed from the word

parts.note: Reds was a name for Soviet-era Russian communists
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A cocktail recipe for Black Russians gone wrong, with bases off.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed is a foundation or base, as in a bed of concrete or a riverbed.

clue.text: From a gin and tonic, drunk moves in a line?

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and jumbled, so the letters of the preceding phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: After a G&T, a tipsy person moves along in a straight line, as a sobriety test.
explanation.definitionFit: This is ballroom dancing performed by teams in set patterns, so dancers move in lines and figures.

clue.text: Tend to go over to escort, getting one's end away

indicators.note: over says the word for go is turned around

parts.note: to run is to go

indicators.note: the escort word loses its own last letter

parts.note: to see someone home is to escort them

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of someone escorting a date and getting lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting one's end away' is British slang for having sex, but here it simply removes the final E of SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To care for the sick or look after something is to tend it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: More Bloody Marys in the middle and one on right

indicators.note: in the middle picks the central letter of Marys

parts.note: a is one
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Ordering more Bloody Marys, with one put on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that is bloody is cooked less, so the comparative of underdone steak fits more bloody.

clue.text: Is tequila shot revealing features?

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a tequila shot reveals someone's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Attributes or characteristics of a thing are its features, a plain synonym.

clue.text: South American cocaine in flower and plant

parts.note: SA is short for South America

indicators.note: in places the drug letter within the river

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Nile
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: A South American hiding cocaine in a flower and a plant, a smuggling scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' reads as a bloom, but in crosswords it is a river (that which flows).
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woodland herb of the carrot family, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Paddy drinks up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up says the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: ports are fortified wines, drinks from Portugal

explanation.surface: Someone called Paddy finishes his drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like a name, but in British usage it means a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A sulk or tantrum is a paddy in British slang, and also a strop.

clue.text: Hearts or clubs? King inserted into decks

indicators.note: inserted into says the two letters go inside the word for decks

parts.note: decks are levels or tiers, as on a ship or bus
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A card game: hearts or clubs, with a king slipped into the decks.
explanation.walkthrough: The card suits mislead: 'Hearts' is the definition and 'clubs' gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal slang for the heart, so the plural matches hearts.

clue.text: Has ink come off? Draw without stopping?

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist asks whether the ink has come off while drawing continuously.
explanation.definitionFit: To light one cigarette from the last is to keep drawing on smoke continuously, the question mark marking the pun on draw.

clue.text: Have casual sex and drink around noon

indicators.note: around says the drink word encloses the noon letter

parts.note: a swig is a gulp of drink

explanation.surface: A lunchtime of drinking and casual sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Swinging is slang for partner-swapping, so the verb means to have casual sex.

clue.text: Had party finish off sangria (five parts wine)

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so the wine word is divided by the letters

parts.note: red is red wine

indicators.note: finish off picks the final letter of sangria

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A recipe for sangria: five parts wine, to finish off a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To rave is to attend a wild party, so the past tense means had a party.

clue.text: Part of Manhattan so nearly opening

indicators.note: nearly drops the last letter

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
a mouth is an opening, as of a river or cave

explanation.surface: A spot in Manhattan, New York, that is almost opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manhattan' is the cocktail, not the borough: the fortified wine is one of its ingredients.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan cocktail is whiskey with the fortified wine and bitters, so it is an ingredient of the drink.

clue.text: Drink with friend

definitions.meaning: Budweiser beer, often shortened in the US
American slang for a pal or mate

explanation.surface: Having a drink with a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a short name for a Budweiser beer and also informal slang for a mate.

clue.text: Ingredient of snowball cocktail that might float in can?

indicators.note: Ingredient of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cocktail recipe: what is in a Snowball, something that floats in a can?
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is slang for a toilet, whose cistern holds a floating valve.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating valve in a toilet cistern controls refilling, and can is informal for lavatory.

clue.text: Like it? One drink

parts.note: as means like
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Do you like it? Have one drink.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a variant name for the açaí berry juice, a drink.

clue.text: Serving men who drop round, left something in a piña colada?

parts.note: paras are paratroopers, soldiers who drop by parachute
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Waiters drop round and leave something in a piña colada.
explanation.definitionFit: A small paper umbrella decorates a tropical cocktail, so it is something found in that drink.

clue.text: See 9
Old records entertaining parties

indicators.note: entertaining means holding inside, so the records word contains the letter

parts.note: discs are records

explanation.surface: Old vinyl records played to entertain parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Dance parties with recorded music are discos, so the plural is a synonym.

clue.text: Wearing ring that's mounted and embedded

parts.note: in means wearing, as in in a suit

indicators.note: mounted means going up, so the word reads upward in a down entry

parts.note: to ring is to dial a phone

explanation.surface: Wearing a ring that has a mounted stone set into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Set into a surface as decoration means embedded, as with inlaid wood.

clue.text: They do up house: home counties housing spikes

indicators.note: housing means containing, so SE encloses the house letters

parts.note: SE is south-east England; the home counties are the counties around London
to lace a drink is to spike it

explanation.surface: Renovators doing up a house in the home counties, with spikes in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They do up' suggests decorators; it means things that fasten shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Strings that tie a shoe fasten it, and to do up is to fasten.

clue.text: Downed one Sex on the Beach?

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above

parts.note: a beach is sand
a lark is a frolic or bit of fun

explanation.surface: Someone knocked back a Sex on the Beach cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downed' suggests drinking, but means covered in down: a bird. Sex on the Beach is a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A shore bird is covered in soft feathers, so it is literally a downy creature.

clue.text: See 24
Article on whisky island

indicators.note: on places the article after the whisky in an across answer

parts.note: malt is malt whisky
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article on an island's whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Mediterranean island nation, so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: No head on men's drinks

indicators.note: no head on means the first letter is removed

parts.note: men are males

explanation.surface: Men's drinks with no frothy head on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Beers are drinks, so the plural noun is an example of drinks.

clue.text: One records who pays for work on Buckingham Palace?

definitions.meaning: someone who writes down or records things

definitions.text: who pays for work on Buckingham Palace?
definitions.meaning: read as a negative followed by the Queen's cipher, Elizabeth Regina: the payer is anyone but the monarch

explanation.surface: Asking who records the payments for repairs to the royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NOT ER: the British taxpayer, not the monarch, funds palace repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes notes is a recorder, so the noun fits one who records.
